You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Nike Q1 Earnings Preview: 12-Year Low Stress Test Hinges on China and Gross Margin

TEXT:
🔥 US Stock Hotspot Radar is Live! Content: 3 major themes + 6 selected stocks + 7 key events. Where are this week’s opportunities? Click the link to see all 22 trading directions in one chart →
Investment Snapshot
Nike ( NKE .US) will report fiscal 2027 first-quarter results (quarter ended August 31) after the U.S. close on October 1, 2026, with the call around 5:00 p.m. ET. Management guided for a low-to-mid-single-digit revenue decline, no FX tailwind, and a “slightly positive” year-over-year gross margin. Street consensus is about $11.32–$11.35 billion in revenue (about -3.2% to -3.4% YoY vs. $11.720 billion a year ago) and EPS of about $0.44 (about -10.2% YoY vs. $0.49). The stock is near $36, down roughly 40% year to date, and was removed from the S&P 100 on September 21 (it remains in the S&P 500). The test is not a return to high growth. It is whether underlying gross margin and Greater China can stabilize after one-offs.
Four Things to Watch
Focus 1: Can the China decline narrow?
Greater China FY26 revenue was $5.847 billion (-11% YoY reported, -13% currency-neutral). Q4 was about $1.29 billion (about -12% reported, about -17% currency-neutral). Sell-side segment consensus for this quarter is still about $1.3 billion (about -12.6% YoY). That is a market estimate, not company segment guidance. Watch inventory, discounts, and full-price sales, not just the top-line drop. Management said China inventory was down double digits and some stores and running improved, but near-term trends should stay close to recent performance. A clearly smaller decline could repair sentiment first. Another print near Q4’s -17% currency-neutral pace would push the turnaround story out again.
Focus 2: Can underlying gross margin actually turn positive?
Last quarter’s reported gross margin was 49.2% (+890 bps YoY), but about 900 bps came from roughly $986 million in tariff recovery. Ex that, margin was only 40.2% (-10 bps YoY), and adjusted EPS was about $0.20 versus reported EPS of $0.72. The Q1 “margin turn” refers to underlying gross margin. Do not compare against 49.2%. Quality markers are full-price mix, discounting, and product mix. This is the number most likely to move the stock.
Focus 3: Can North America offset the rest of the world?
Q4 North America revenue was about $4.83 billion (+3% YoY), with wholesale stronger and Direct still weak. Sell-side segment consensus this quarter: North America about $5.1 billion (about +2% YoY); EMEA about $3.2 billion (about -4% YoY); APLA about $1.4 billion (about -3% YoY); footwear about $7.2 billion (about -3% YoY). Converse was about $244 million last quarter (about -32% YoY); this quarter’s consensus is about $296 million (about -19% YoY). If wholesale shipments outrun sell-through, inventory cleanup remains a risk.
Focus 4: Q2 slowdown and the full-year gap
Management already flagged Q2 as slower than Q1, mainly on a tough EMEA digital-promo compare and North America wholesale timing. FY26 revenue was $46.4 billion (flat reported, about -2% currency-neutral). Reported EPS was $2.10, or about $1.58 ex tariff recovery. FY27 consensus revenue is about $45.3–$45.7 billion (around -2% YoY), with EPS around $1.65–$1.66. Some firms are well below that and see a sales inflection only in FY28. The November 16–17 Investor Day is the real midterm strategy check.
Risk and Opportunity
Upside catalysts:
Group decline better than mid-single digits, and China’s currency-neutral drop narrower than Q4.
Underlying gross margin turns positive, with cleaner discounts and inventory.
North America wholesale matches sell-through, and management does not cut the first-half outlook.
Downside risks:
China or Converse worsens and widens the group decline.
Margin does not turn, or growth is bought with promotions.
Q2 is confirmed weaker and the recovery is pushed out again; a low price is not a floor.
Trading Framework
Bull case: The revenue decline stays contained, underlying gross margin turns positive, and China shows signs that the worst quarter is in. Dip buyers may treat that as phase two of the reset.
Bear case: Results meet guidance but quality is poor (heavy discounting, weak Direct, unhealthy inventory), or management explicitly delays the inflection.
Key data:
Total revenue and YoY growth (reported / currency-neutral)
Greater China revenue, inventory, and discounts
Gross margin ex one-offs
North America wholesale vs. Direct and sell-through
Q2 and full-year commentary, plus Investor Day preview
Tactical notes (as of the September 29 close at $35.84):
Pre-print: Range-bound between $35.22 and $37.04. Made a 52-week low at $35.22 on September 25 and closed $35.84 on September 29. 20-day MA $36.78, 50-day MA $39.38, 200-day MA $49.21. Resistance: $36.67 / $36.78 / $37.04 / $39.38. Support: $35.67 / $35.22 / $35.00 / $34.20. Options imply about ±8.7%–9.0% (roughly $32.6–$39.1). Keep size light. No leveraged longs below $35.22.
Long setup: Daily close back above $36.78–$37.04, with pullbacks holding $35.22. Upside reference $39.38. Stop $35.00.
Short setup: Break of $35.22, or a bounce that fails $36.78. Downside references $35.00 / $34.20 / $32.60.
Playbook: Trade margin and China quality, not whether revenue turns positive. If the print beats on quality, wait for a retest of $35.22–$36.78. If results are mixed or guidance is soft, do not buy the dip. Watch IV crush. Size and stops must match your own risk tolerance.
Disclaimer: For information only. Not investment advice.
